title: Peptide unit converter
formula: 1 mg = 1000 mcg = 1000000 ng, fixed ratios. millilitres to syringe units = volume (mL) x units per mL on the chosen scale (100, 50 or 40). International units are deliberately not converted: an IU is defined per substance by an international reference preparation, so micrograms per IU differ by compound and exist only where a factor has been published.
summary: Converts between milligrams, micrograms and nanograms, and converts a volume into units on a U-100, U-50 or U-40 syringe. It refuses to convert international units, because no general mass equivalent for an IU exists and any converter offering one has invented it.
open_questions: Whether to accept a user-supplied IU factor for a named compound, which would be honest arithmetic but could be mistaken for the site endorsing that factor.

changelog.change: Record created so the tool can be indexed. The calculator itself was rebuilt the same day: the unit converter and vial planner had no calculator at all, only a description.
